articles.headline: OFAC Designates Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations for Narcotics and Terrorism
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting several Guatemalan drug trafficking organizations (DTOs) under counter narcotics and counter terrorism authorities. The designated entities include LOS LORENZANAS (also known as LORENZANA DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION, "THE LORENZANA CLAN," and "THE LORENZANA FAMILY"), LOS MENDOZA DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION, and LOS HUISTAS DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION.

LOS LORENZANAS was designated as a Transnational Terrorist Group and Criminal Organization, with secondary sanctions risk under Executive Order 13224, as amended by Executive Order 13886. LOS MENDOZA DTO, operating in Guatemala, Honduras, and Belize, and LOS HUISTAS DTO, based in various locations in Huehuetenango, Guatemala, were also designated as Criminal Organizations with similar secondary sanctions risks.

These actions aim to disrupt the financial and logistical support provided by these Guatemalan networks to Mexican cartels, including the Sinaloa Cartel and Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generación, in their illicit drug trafficking operations.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran-Related SDN Listing for Volta Shipping Services LLC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an update to an Iran-related designation on November 9, 2026, specifically modifying the entry for Volta Shipping Services LLC.
The update changed the listed alias for the UAE-based company, linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani, from Volta Shipping Services FZCO to Volta Container Line FZCO.
Volta Shipping Services LLC remains designated under Executive Order 13902 and continues to be subject to secondary sanctions risk.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Eight Canada-Based Money Services Businesses for Iran-Related Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced sanctions on November 6, 2026, targeting eight Canada-based money services businesses (MSBs) for their involvement in facilitating transactions for Iran.

These businesses are accused of operating within the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy, including converting Iranian currency into digital assets and conducting transactions with sanctioned Iranian exchanges and digital asset addresses linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

This action, part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' and coordinated with FinCEN and Canada's FINTRAC, was taken under Executive Order 13902 to target international financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-Related and Transnational Criminal Organizations; Expands Cuba Sanctions
body: On November 5, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting cyber-related actors and transnational criminal organizations, alongside significant expansions to its Cuba sanctions program.

The Cuba designations were accompanied by the publication of a Cuba-related determination, extending Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine.

This action allows the U.S. government to block property of non-U.S. persons determined to operate in these newly designated sectors, increasing compliance obligations and enforcement risks for companies with dealings in Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Alert on Shadow Fleet, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, alongside updates to certain Iran-related listings.

As part of this action, OFAC published an Iran-related alert concerning the Iranian 'shadow fleet' and its reliance on false flags for sanctions evasion, highlighting risks for shipping and maritime stakeholders.
Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and an updated Frequently Asked Question, providing revised guidance for transactions involving Venezuela.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License FF-1 for International Development Bank
body: On October 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Iran General License FF-1, titled "Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance."

This amended general license provides authorization for the wind-down of specific transactions, offering guidance for entities involved with the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.
The issuance is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to manage and clarify the scope of its Iran sanctions program.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Bank Data Insights

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals for North Korea and DRC-Related Activities
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)-related activities.

Among the North Korea-related additions are Russian and North Korean nationals linked to LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ALIS, CHINYONG INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY COOPERATION COMPANY, and FIRST FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT CENTER, with listed digital currency addresses on Ethereum and TRON.
The DRC-related designations include Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Kigali-based financial institution, for their support of the M23 group.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026, totaling $1,529,685.

The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations, stemming from Extreme Networks' export of networking equipment and services to a Russian defense manufacturer, Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA).

MMZA was deemed a blocked person by operation of law due to its majority ownership by designated entity JSC Concern Almaz-Antey, even though MMZA itself was not on the SDN List at the time of the transactions. OFAC determined the violations were egregious but voluntarily self-disclosed.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) as part of its ongoing review of published guidance.
The updated FAQs, specifically numbers 10, 32-36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, address topics related to blocking and rejecting transactions, as well as filing reports with OFAC.

These amendments aim to ensure that information remains current and provide clearer explanations on procedures for financial institutions and other entities regarding sanctions compliance, including when to block versus reject transactions and reporting obligations.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Sanctions Law Center

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026.
Concurrently, OFAC issued designations removals related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions against these countries.
The action also included the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, along with amended Frequently Asked Questions, providing updated guidance for various transactions.

articles.headline: EU Agrees to 113 New Russia Sanctions Listings and Targets Cyber Activities
body: The European Union is set to agree on 113 new sanctions listings targeting Russia, as confirmed by Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee.
These new listings are part of ongoing discussions for a broader 22nd sanctions package against Moscow.

Additionally, the Council decided to add 30 individuals and two entities to the list of those subject to EU restrictive measures for Russia's malicious cyber activities and foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI).

articles.headline: UK Adds 20 Entities to Russia Sanctions List, Imposes Transport Sanctions
body: On November 12, 2026, the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated the UK Sanctions List, adding 20 new entities and one variation under the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019.
Among the additions is JSC NIPIGAZPERERABOTKA, which is now subject to asset freeze, trust services sanctions, director disqualification sanctions, and transport sanctions.

The transport sanctions prohibit ships and aircraft owned, controlled, chartered, or operated by designated persons from entering or overflying the UK, and also include prohibitions on providing technical assistance related to such vessels.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Fined $1,529,685 by OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-headquartered cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services on nine occasions to Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer.

MMZA was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by designated entity JSC Concern Almaz Antey, even though MMZA itself was not directly listed on the SDN List at the time of the transactions. OFAC determined the violations were egregious but voluntarily self-disclosed.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
